one_liner: Skia's small ICC colour-management library (parse profiles, SIMD pixel transforms); no published speed comparison against Little CMS.
what_it_does: skcms parses ICC profiles (TRC plus matrix, A2B/B2A LUTs, CICP with PQ and HLG) and converts pixel buffers between profiles and pixel formats (8-bit, 565, 4444, 1010102, 16-bit LE/BE, half and single float, 10-bit XR). The API is a plain C interface in skcms.h: skcms_Parse() fills an skcms_ICCProfile that points into your buffer, and skcms_Transform(src, srcFmt, srcAlpha, srcProfile, dst, dstFmt, dstAlpha, dstProfile, npixels) does the conversion in one call. It is not a drop-in for lcms2: there is no cmsHTRANSFORM object, no rendering-intent or black-point-compensation parameters, and destinations must be parametric-TRC or B2A profiles.
how_it_is_fast: Each skcms_Transform call compiles a short program of at most 32 ops (load, curves, matrix or CLUT, clamp, premul, store) and runs it over float vectors of 4 (SSE/NEON/LSX/WASM), 8 (AVX2+F16C, 'hsw') or 16 (AVX-512, 'skx') lanes, picked by a one-time cpuid/xgetbv check. Stages are chained with [[clang::musttail]] tail calls where the compiler supports it, transfer functions use approximate log2/exp2 (approx_pow) instead of powf, the source and destination gamut matrices are concatenated into one 3x3, an identical gamut skips the matrix, and LUT/CLUT lookups use AVX2/AVX-512 gathers and hardware half-float conversion.
when_to_use: You already build Skia or Chromium-style code and want the same colour conversions they ship, with no new dependency.
Decoding images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL) whose embedded ICC or CICP profile must be converted to sRGB or a display profile, row by row.
HDR pipelines that need PQ and HLG transfer functions, including the HLG OOTF, plus half-float and 10-bit XR output formats.
Many pixel formats in one library without writing per-format packing code; 255-pixel or larger batches, so the per-call planning cost is amortised.
Untrusted ICC input: the repo carries libFuzzer targets (fuzz/fuzz_iccprofile_info.c, fuzz/fuzz_iccprofile_transform.c), and skcms.cc never calls malloc, so parsing does not allocate or copy.
when_not_to_use: You need lcms2 features: rendering intents beyond the A2B0/A2B1 preference, black point compensation, proofing, device links, named colours or multi-profile chains.

Destination profiles with tabulated TRCs: they must be rewritten by skcms_MakeUsableAsDestination(), which fits a parametric curve and fails or approximates badly on some profiles (tests.c lists several).
You need bit-exact or lcms2-identical output: transfer functions run through approx_pow, and the repo's own A2B round-trip test tolerates 1/255 error (9/255 at zero).
You picked it for speed: no benchmark against Little CMS, its fast_float plugin, qcms or moxcms is published, and bench.c only times skcms itself.
General CMYK workflows: CMYK is handled as Photoshop-style inverted CMYK only (the code says those are the only CMYK profiles it has seen).

integration.form: source-drop (skcms.cc plus src/*.cc and headers); ninja and Bazel builds produce a static library
integration.min_toolchain: C++ with lambdas and constexpr (C++11 level; the exact standard is not documented); Clang or GCC vector extensions for the SIMD paths, otherwise SKCMS_PORTABLE scalar code (for example MSVC without clang-cl)
integration.platforms: x86-64 with runtime dispatch to SSE baseline, AVX2+F16C or AVX-512 (AVX2/AVX-512 paths disabled on Android); aarch64 and armv7 NEON; LoongArch LSX; WebAssembly SIMD via Emscripten; ppc64le and RISC-V without musttail; Windows without musttail
integration.thread_safety: not documented; from the code, skcms_Transform keeps no shared mutable state apart from a one-time CPU-detection static, so concurrent calls with read-only profiles look safe, and parsed profiles borrow the caller's ICC buffer

gotchas: skcms_Transform has no cached transform object: every call re-plans the pipeline (including inverting the destination transfer functions), so very small calls pay setup each time.
Passing the same profile pointer as source and destination skips the colour conversion entirely (only format conversion runs); any benchmark against lcms2 that does this is not like for like.
skcms_ICCProfile points into the ICC buffer passed to skcms_Parse(); the buffer must outlive the profile.

bench.c times skcms on static float buffers that are never filled (all-zero pixels) and rotates pixel formats each iteration, so its ns-per-pixel figure is a profiling aid, not a throughput number for real images.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick skcms over the Little-CMS fast_float plugin when you want a small, dependency-free, fuzzed C/C++ library matching Skia and Chromium output and can live without lcms2's intents and device links; pick moxcms instead in Rust code, where it at least publishes timings against lcms2. Keep lcms2 plus fast_float when you need the full ICC feature set or measured speed.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing comparative has been measured: neither README makes a speed claim, and bench.c (mirror branch) only prints skcms's own ns per pixel for 255-pixel batches of sRGB to a Display P3 matrix, which its header calls 'mostly to run in a profiler'. imazen/cms-bench has a zenbench harness timing moxcms, skcms and lcms2 on 8-bit, 16-bit, float and LUT profiles but commits no results; in its identity group skcms gets the same profile pointer twice (no colour math), and only the skcms rows include per-call setup.
status_note: The GitHub repo is a read-only mirror whose last sync is 2025-09-16 ('Disable must_tail on GCC when compiling for RISC-V'), so it reads as stale even though upstream on skia.googlesource.com is likely still used by Skia and Chromium; BSD-3-Clause and small enough to vendor.
